- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overbought trap.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.8) and price is trending up, model often underestimates momentum — increase forecast by 2-5% for next 3-5 days to capture sentiment-driven rally.  
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1-3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to short-term forecast if sentiment swings >1.0.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +1.0, -2.0, +1.0), model tends to lag — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum, especially if price is trending.  
- Avoid overfitting to recent history — if last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2 consecutive drops >1.5%), model should not forecast further decline — instead, forecast a slight rebound or flat.
